who: Historian of Canadian environmental history, York University; history PhD dissertation submitted at York in 2007.

evidence.says: The 2013–14 faculty list identifies Sean R. Kheraj as assistant professor of history with MA and PhD from York.
Dissertation title page: Sean Rizwan Ribeirinho Kheraj, Inventing Nature’s Past: An Environmental History of Stanley Park, PhD in History, York University, 2007.
Inventing Stanley Park (2013) is by Sean Kheraj, identified as an assistant professor of history at York.
The authority identifies Sean Kheraj through Inventing Stanley Park (2013).

notes: The authority’s book author matches the York historian and the AHA doctoral institution; the 2007 date is the dissertation title-page date.

who: Historian of American politics, Michigan State University, 1994–2009; PhD American history, Johns Hopkins, 1988.

evidence.says: Fall 2009 college magazine identifies incoming dean Mark Kornbluh as formerly Michigan State history professor and chair, with a 1988 doctorate in American history from Johns Hopkins.
Wayne State’s announcement states that Mark L. Kornbluh taught at Michigan State from 1994 to 2009.
Why America Stopped Voting identifies author Mark Lawrence Kornbluh as associate professor of history at Michigan State.
The authority identifies Mark Lawrence Kornbluh as author of Why America Stopped Voting.

notes: Full name, book, Michigan State employment through the students’ 2009 graduation, and doctoral institution/year agree.

who: Historian of modern Russia and Soviet gender history, Duke University; PhD Johns Hopkins.

evidence.says: Duke identifies Anna Krylova as a historian of modern Russia and associate professor of history since 2010; the Education section lists a Johns Hopkins PhD in 2000.
Duke attributes Soviet Women in Combat: A History of Violence on the Eastern Front to Anna Krylova.
The authority identifies Anna Krylova through Soviet Women in Combat (2010).

notes: Institution, field, doctorate and book agree. Duke’s overview gives the PhD year as 2001, while its Education section gives 2000, matching AHA; retain this source discrepancy.

notes: Direct supervision evidence names both AHA students; degree and authority-linked book also agree.

who: Historian of African American urban history and social movements, formerly Illinois faculty; PhD Illinois, 2004.

evidence.says: Illinois’s repository names Clarence E. Lang as research director and doctoral committee chair for Stephanie Seawell’s 2014 history PhD dissertation.
Illinois identifies Clarence Lang as a 2004 PhD alumnus.
Penn State identifies Lang’s field as African American urban history and social movements and lists his co-edited Anticommunism and the African American Freedom Movement.
The authority identifies Clarence Lang through Anticommunism and the African American Freedom Movement (2009).

notes: Repository supervision, degree and authority-linked publication confirm the identity.

who: Historian of modern France and Germany, Stony Brook University; PhD Yale, 1965.

evidence.says: His 2015 institutional CV lists a Yale PhD in 1965, Stony Brook faculty employment from 1966 onward, and True France (1992) and The Alliance of Iron and Wheat (1988).
The authority identifies Herman Lebovics through True France and The Alliance of Iron and Wheat.

notes: Doctorate, faculty employment covering both students’ years, and two authority-linked works agree.

who: Historian of ancient and medieval history at Mississippi State University; mentor of Larry Usilton.

evidence.says: UNCW’s profile of Larry Usilton identifies his mentor as Mississippi State professor Charles Lewis, who encouraged his interest in ancient and medieval history.
Charlene Marie Boyer Lewis’s CV lists a University of Virginia PhD in 1997, Kalamazoo faculty employment from 2002, and Ladies and Gentlemen on Display (2001).
The authority identifies Charlene M. Boyer Lewis through Ladies and Gentlemen on Display.
Charlton Thomas Lewis was a Latin lexicographer, professor of Greek at Troy University in 1858–61, and co-author of A Latin Dictionary (1879).
The Naval Academy identifies Charles Lee Lewis as its English and history professor from 1916 to retirement in 1951, author of naval biographies and Famous American Naval Officers (1924).

notes: Reject all three: p-100567 is Charlene Boyer Lewis, with a different name and doctorate; p-132366 is the nineteenth-century lexicographer Charlton Thomas Lewis; p-130263 is naval historian Charles Lee Lewis. None matches the Mississippi State medieval-history supervisor.

who: Historian of Cuba, the Caribbean and immigration, Rutgers University since 2009; PhD University of Michigan.

evidence.says: Rutgers identifies Kathleen Lopez as associate professor of Latino and Caribbean Studies and History, at Rutgers since 2009, with a Michigan PhD; her publication is Chinese Cubans: A Transnational History (2013).
The authority identifies Kathleen López through Chinese Cubans (2013).

notes: Name variant, field, Rutgers affiliation during both students’ years, Michigan doctorate and authority-linked book agree.
